answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, while a shared evidence kernel correlates equivocations across keys. If k coordinated identities sign conflicting histories, the protocol aggregates their violations and applies penalties scaling as O(k^2), rather than treating each as an isolated fault. On detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss makes a hollow swarm costly to maintain; splitting keys cannot let an operator wander beyond the linked collateral and slashing record.
